name: SSC MTS
fullName: Staff Selection Commission – Multi-Tasking (Non-Technical) Staff and Havaldar (CBIC & CBN) Examination
approxCandidates: Tens of lakhs of applicants per cycle (official 2026 figure not available at check time)
eligibility: Class 10 (matriculation) pass; 18–25 years for MTS and 18–27 years for Havaldar and some MTS posts (with category relaxations)

notification.summary: The SSC 2026-27 calendar listed the MTS & Havaldar 2026 notification for 30 June 2026 with the CBT in Sep–Nov 2026, but as of 10 Oct 2026 it had not been confirmed as released; reports say it was postponed and is now expected around October 2026. The previous (2025) cycle had ≈7,948 posts, CBT held 4–15 Feb 2026 and Havaldar PET/PST in late Aug 2026.

importantDates.date: Calendar window Sep–Nov 2026; likely to shift (to be announced)

notification.source: https://www.adda247.com/ssc-mts (secondary report; official notices at https://ssc.gov.in)

pattern.stage: Computer Based Examination (Session I + Session II)
pattern.notes: Two sessions of 45 minutes each, both compulsory. Session I (Numerical + Reasoning) has NO negative marking and is qualifying; Session II (GA + English) has −1 per wrong answer and decides merit. Each question carries 3 marks. Havaldar candidates also take a PET/PST. The paper is available in English, Hindi and 13 regional languages.

trendAnalysis.summary: The MTS CBT is easy-to-moderate. Session I tests basic arithmetic (number system, percentage, profit & loss, ratio, average, time-work, speed and simple mensuration) and verbal/non-verbal reasoning (analogy, classification, series, coding, directions, blood relations). Session II decides merit: GA is mostly static GK (history, polity, geography, science, culture, sports) with a few current-affairs questions, and English covers vocabulary, basic grammar (articles, prepositions, tenses, subject–verb agreement) and a short comprehension/cloze. Because of the −1 penalty in Session II, accuracy in GA and English separates selected candidates.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the commission's published question-paper/response-sheet format and from shift-wise memory-based papers and topic-wise analyses published by coaching sites (Testbook, Adda247, PW, Careers360 day-wise analyses) for the 2023–2025 cycles, cross-checked against the writer's own knowledge of SSC papers. Live web fetches during this round returned only summary pages (SSC barred public discussion of 2025 papers), so question-type detail relies mainly on prior knowledge of the papers; frequencies are approximate per-shift counts. Figure-based (non-verbal) archetypes are recorded but only text-renderable variants are used for generated questions.

archetypes.pattern: Word-pair analogy (A : B :: C : ?) built on a semantic relation – worker : tool, product : raw material, organ : function, instrument : quantity measured, young one : animal; distractors are words of the same category that do not share the relation.

Number-pair/triad analogy where the second term comes from an arithmetic rule on the first (n² ± k, n³ ± k, ×k ± c, digit operations); often framed with two example pairs and a note to operate on whole numbers without splitting digits; distractors satisfy the rule for only one pair or come from ±1 slips.
Letter-cluster analogy (ABCD : EFGH :: ? ) where each letter moves by a fixed or alternating +/− shift or is replaced by its opposite letter (A↔Z); distractors differ in exactly one letter.
Odd-one-out among four words/objects by category or property (three belong to one class, e.g. instruments, organs, rivers of one state); the trap is a surface feature shared by the odd item.
Odd number / number-pair / triad out of four where three follow one arithmetic rule (squares, primes, (a, b, c) with c = a×b − k, divisibility); the odd option breaks the rule by a small margin.
Odd letter-cluster out of four where three clusters have the same positional gaps (e.g. +2, +3 or opposite-letter pairs) and one breaks the gap pattern.
Number series with one missing/next term following a two-step rule (×k + c, alternating operations, differences forming squares/primes or their own series).

Letter or alphanumeric cluster series (e.g. three-letter groups with each position advancing by its own increment, possibly mixed with numbers); find the next cluster; distractors shift one position wrongly.
Word → letter code by a positional rule (each letter shifted by +k/−k, alternate shifts, reversal then shift, or opposite letters); decode the rule from one example and encode a new word.

Word → number code from alphabet positions (sum of positions, sum × k, sum of reverse positions, number of letters × k); apply the rule to a new word; distractors use forward instead of reverse positions.
Sentence coding: two or three short sentences coded as groups of code words; identify the code of a given word by finding the common word/code between statements.
Verbal chain / introduction ('pointing to a photo…') blood relation: trace 3–4 links and name the relation; traps are gender assumptions and the paternal/maternal side.
Coded blood relations: symbols (A + B, A × B, A − B …) stand for relations; decode an expression to find how two people are related, or which expression makes a given relation true.

Walking path of 3–5 legs with left/right turns; find the shortest distance and/or direction from the start (often a Pythagorean triple); or the final facing direction after a sequence of left/right/clockwise turns; traps are direction after a 'right turn' and adding instead of subtracting legs.
Two/three statements ('All/Some/No') with two conclusions; decide which follow, including 'Some … are not' and possibility-type conclusions; trap is reversing 'All A are B'.
Symbol substitution: '+' means '×', '−' means '÷' etc.; rewrite and evaluate an expression with BODMAS; distractors come from left-to-right evaluation.
Which two signs (or two numbers) must be interchanged to make a given equation correct; each option names a pair of signs to swap.
Missing term inside a number sequence (often the middle term) built from a mixed rule such as ×1 + 1, ×2 + 2, ×3 + 3 … or alternating × and +; find the term that replaces '?'.
Defined-operation missing number: from two or three solved examples (a ★ b = …) infer the rule (a² + b², (a + b)², a×b + a …) and apply it; distractors fit just one example.

Position from both ends: total in a row/class from two ranks, rank from the other end, persons between two people, or a short comparison chain (taller/older) to find who is at a rank; trap is ±1 counting.
Calendar: day of the week for a date given a reference date (odd-days counting across leap years) or after n days.
Clock angle between the hands at a given time (30H − 5.5M) or time when hands coincide/are opposite.
Mirror image of a clock time or of an alphanumeric/number string (vertical mirror on the right); time question solved by 11:60 − time.
A square sheet is folded once or twice and punched/cut; predict how it looks (number/position of holes) when unfolded.
Count triangles/squares in a figure built from a square or triangle with diagonals and mid-lines.

Ancient and medieval India: dynasty founders, capitals, rulers' titles, Buddhist/Jain councils, Delhi Sultanate/Mughal/Vijayanagara rulers, battles with years and administrative reforms; distractors are rulers of the same or adjacent dynasty.
Modern India and freedom struggle: founders of organisations/newspapers, INC sessions and presidents, movements with years, Governors-General and their acts.
Article-number question: which Article deals with a given provision (FR, DPSP, office, emergency, finance); distractors are nearby Article numbers.
Constitution-making, Preamble, amendments, schedules and parts with their subject matter (e.g. which Schedule/amendment added X); distractors are adjacent schedules/amendments.
Constitutional/statutory offices: appointment, qualification (age), tenure, removal, oath, and borrowed features of the Constitution.
Indian physical geography: rivers (origin, tributaries, states), lakes, passes, hills, national parks and their states.
Soils, crops, minerals, climate and resources of India (which soil/crop/mineral/region; seasons and winds).
World/physical geography: atmosphere layers, ocean currents, straits, planets, latitudes and landforms.
Banking and monetary policy: RBI instruments (repo, CRR, SLR), functions, institutions and their headquarters.
Economic concepts and planning: GDP/GNP, deficits, inflation measures, Five-Year Plans, taxes, government schemes and their launch.
Physics: SI units and instruments, and everyday phenomena (mirrors/lenses, dispersion, sound speed, heat, electricity).
Chemistry: common names/formulae of compounds, ores and alloys, acids in foods, pH, gases and periodic-table facts.
Human biology: vitamins/minerals and deficiency diseases, organs and glands, blood, diseases and their causative agents.
Plant biology and classification: tissues, photosynthesis, plant hormones, cell organelles, scientists behind classification.
Performing arts and festivals: classical/folk dances, festivals and fairs with their states, instruments and their maestros.
Temples, monuments and architectural styles with their builders/dynasties and locations.
Recent national/international events of the last 1–2 years: summits and hosts, missions, schemes and major appointments.
Sports: number of players, terms and trophies of a sport, venues, and recent Olympic/Asian Games/World Cup results involving India.
Book–author matching (classical and contemporary, including autobiographies) and literary/national award facts.
Unit digit of a power/product or remainder of a large power on division (cyclicity); distractors are adjacent cycle values.
Divisibility and number properties: smallest digit/number to add or subtract for divisibility by 9, 11, 8, which number is divisible, count of factors, primes, or sum of numbers in a range.
HCF/LCM word problem: largest number dividing with given remainders, bells tolling together, least number leaving the same remainder, or HCF × LCM = product.
BODMAS simplification with fractions/decimals/brackets or 'value of ?' equations; distractors come from wrong operation order.
Basic/successive percentage: x% of a number, net effect of successive increases/decreases, or price rise vs consumption cut.
Percentage word problems: election votes, pass-fail marks, salary spent/saved; find the total or the difference.
Marked price above cost with a discount (or successive discounts) – find profit % or marked price.
Cost/selling price relation: profit % from CP and SP, CP from SP and gain %, CP of x items = SP of y items, two articles sold at the same price, or false-weight dealers.
Simple interest: find rate/time/principal from amounts, or the time to become n times.
Compound interest for 2–3 years, CI − SI difference, or half-yearly compounding.
Divide an amount in a given (sometimes fractional) ratio, or find shares/partnership profit.
Ratio change: number added/subtracted to change a ratio, combined ratio A : B : C, or mean/third proportional.
Average: simple or consecutive-number averages, inclusion/exclusion/replacement of a member (teacher's age, wrong entry corrected), or overlap of first-k and last-k averages.
Two/three workers with individual days; together, one leaves after some days, or efficiency ratio problems.
Pipes and cisterns (filling and emptying pipes together) or men-days (M₁D₁ = M₂D₂) proportionality.
Trains crossing a pole/platform/another train (same or opposite direction) with km/h ↔ m/s conversion.
Average speed for to-and-fro journeys, relative speed/chase problems, or boats and streams.
Triangle properties: angle at incentre/orthocentre, angle-bisector/median length, similarity ratios, Pythagorean right-triangle facts.
Circle theorems: chords intersecting, tangent length, angle in a semicircle, cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles.
2-D mensuration: area/perimeter of rectangles, triangles (Heron's), circles and sectors, change in area with change in dimensions.
3-D mensuration: volume/surface area of cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere/hemisphere; melting and recasting.
Factual RC question on a 150–250-word passage: answer is stated in the passage; distractors use passage words with altered meaning.
Inference/main-idea/title RC question: choose the central theme or what the author implies.
Vocabulary/tone in context: synonym/antonym of a word used in the passage or the author's tone.
Cloze passage with five numbered blanks; each item tests contextual vocabulary, a connector or a preposition; distractors are near-synonyms that fail the collocation.
Single-sentence blank requiring the contextually correct word (collocation, near-synonym choice).
Single-sentence blank testing grammar – prepositions, articles, tense, conjunctions.
Synonym of a standalone or underlined word (moderate CGL-level vocabulary); distractors include antonyms and look-alike words.
Antonym of a standalone or underlined word; the trap option is a synonym of the given word.
Meaning of a common idiom/phrase (or the idiom that fits a sentence); distractors are literal readings.
One-word substitute for a descriptive phrase (persons, -cide, -phobia, -archy words); distractors are related words of the same family.
Select the correctly (or incorrectly) spelt word among four look-alike spellings (double letters, ie/ei, -ance/-ence).
Sentence split into 3–4 segments; error in subject–verb agreement, pronoun or noun number (each/one of/neither…nor, uncountable nouns).
Sentence split into segments; error in tense sequence, preposition, comparative/superlative, or conjunction pairs (hardly…when, no sooner…than).
Improve the bracketed/underlined part: tense, conditional, preposition or idiom usage; 'No improvement' sometimes an option.
Change active to passive (or vice versa) across tenses, including questions and modals; distractors change the tense.

resources.notes: SSC releases tentative answer keys along with each candidate's response sheet (question paper) on ssc.gov.in for a short period after the CBT; there is no permanent official PYQ archive. Shift-wise memory-based papers are compiled by coaching sites.

questions.question: What is the smallest number that must be added to 457 to make it exactly divisible by 9?
questions.explanation: Digit sum of 457 = 16. The next multiple of 9 is 18, so add 2 (459 = 9 × 51).

relevance.note: Smallest addend for divisibility by 9 via digit sum; common MTS number item

questions.question: At what rate of simple interest per annum will ₹2,500 amount to ₹3,100 in 3 years?

relevance.note: Rate from SI amount; standard MTS SI item

questions.question: The average age of 5 boys is 16 years. When their teacher's age is included, the average becomes 20 years. What is the teacher's age?

relevance.note: Teacher's age added to average; very frequent in MTS

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 46 cm and its length is 15 cm. What is its area?

relevance.note: Rectangle area from perimeter; MTS 2-D mensuration
(a²−b²)/(a−b) decimal simplification; MTS staple

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become four times itself at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Doubling means interest = P in 8 years, so rate = 12.5%. Four times needs interest = 3P, which takes 3 × 8 = 24 years.

relevance.note: Doubles in 8 years → 4× in 24 years with 32 trap; MTS SI

questions.question:
Select the number that will come next in the series.
2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?

relevance.note: n²+1 series; MTS series

questions.question:
Select the term that will come next in the series.
AC, EG, IK, MO, ?
questions.explanation: Consecutive odd-position letters: A(1)C(3), E(5)G(7), I(9)K(11), M(13)O(15), then Q(17)S(19).

relevance.note: Alternate-letter pair series; MTS letter series

questions.question:
If '×' means '+', '+' means '÷', '−' means '×' and '÷' means '−', what is the value of:
20 + 4 − 3 × 6 ÷ 2

relevance.note: Sign-substitution BODMAS; MTS

questions.question: In a queue, Amit is 7th from the front and 9th from the back. How many people are in the queue?

relevance.note: Front+back−1 queue count; MTS ranking

questions.question: If today is Wednesday, what day of the week will it be after 100 days?
questions.explanation: 100 = 7 × 14 + 2. Two days after Wednesday is Friday.

relevance.note: Day after 100 days via odd days; MTS calendar

questions.question:
Statements:
Some books are pens.
All pens are pencils.
Conclusions:
I. Some books are pencils.
II. All pencils are pens.
Which conclusion(s) follow(s)?
questions.explanation: The books that are pens are also pencils, so I follows. 'All pens are pencils' does not mean all pencils are pens, so II does not follow.

relevance.note: Some-all syllogism with conversion trap; MTS

questions.question: How many members can the President of India nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under Article 80, the President nominates 12 members with expertise in literature, science, art and social service.

relevance.note: 12 nominated Rajya Sabha members; MTS polity

questions.question: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
questions.explanation: Under Article 60, the oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India (or, in his absence, the senior-most Supreme Court judge).

relevance.note: Oath to President by CJI with VP trap; MTS office item

questions.question: The Preamble declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic ______.
questions.explanation: The Preamble describes India as a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic.

relevance.note: Preamble 'Republic' blank; MTS

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

relevance.note: Article 17 untouchability; MTS article item

questions.question: Loktak Lake, known for its floating 'phumdis', is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Loktak Lake in Manipur has floating phumdis; Keibul Lamjao, the only floating national park, is on it.

relevance.note: Loktak/phumdis–Manipur; MTS geography

questions.question: What is the name of the southernmost point of Indian territory?
questions.explanation: Indira Point on Great Nicobar Island is India's southernmost point; Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of the mainland.

relevance.note: Indira Point southernmost with Kanyakumari trap; MTS

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
HUMBLE
questions.explanation: Humble means modest; its opposite is arrogant.

relevance.note: HUMBLE antonym with Modest/Meek traps; MTS

questions.question:
Select the one-word substitute for the given phrase.
One who does not believe in the existence of God
questions.explanation: An atheist does not believe in God; a theist does.

relevance.note: Atheist vs theist OWS; MTS

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
If it rains tomorrow, we ______ the match.
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + simple present, will + base verb.

relevance.note: First conditional 'will cancel'; MTS

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
She waited for ______ hour at the station.
questions.explanation: 'Hour' begins with a vowel sound (silent h), so the article is 'an'.

relevance.note: Article 'an hour'; MTS grammar blank

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bracketed part of the sentence.
I [am knowing] him for ten years.
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb (not used in continuous form), and an action continuing up to now takes the present perfect: I have known him for ten years.

relevance.note: Stative verb 'have known'; MTS improvement

questions.question: What is the largest 4-digit number that is exactly divisible by 12?
questions.explanation: 9999 ÷ 12 leaves remainder 3, so the largest multiple is 9999 − 3 = 9996.

relevance.note: Largest 4-digit multiple of 12; MTS number

questions.question: What is the unit digit of 2⁴⁷?
questions.explanation: Unit digits of powers of 2 repeat as 2, 4, 8, 6. 47 = 4 × 11 + 3, so the unit digit is 8.

relevance.note: Unit digit of 2^47; MTS cyclicity

questions.question: Three bells toll at intervals of 12, 15 and 20 minutes respectively. If they toll together at 9:00 a.m., at what time will they next toll together?
questions.explanation: LCM of 12, 15 and 20 = 60 minutes, so they next toll together at 10:00 a.m.

relevance.note: Bells toll together via LCM; MTS word problem

questions.question: A shirt is marked at ₹800 and sold at a discount of 15%. If the shopkeeper still makes a profit of 13⅓%, what is the cost price of the shirt?

relevance.note: CP from MP, discount and 13⅓% gain; MTS profit

questions.question: What sum of money will amount to ₹6,600 in 4 years at 5% per annum simple interest?

relevance.note: Principal from SI amount; MTS

questions.question: The average of 6 numbers is 15. If one of the numbers, 20, is removed, what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.explanation: Total = 90. After removing 20, total = 70 for 5 numbers, average = 14.

relevance.note: Average after removing one number; MTS

questions.question: A person travels from his home to his office at 30 km/h and returns along the same route at 20 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation: For equal distances, average speed = 2 × 30 × 20/(30 + 20) = 24 km/h (not the simple average 25).

relevance.note: To-and-fro harmonic average speed with 25 trap; MTS

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word.
Carpenter : Wood :: Tailor : ?
questions.explanation: A carpenter works with wood; a tailor works with cloth. The needle is a tool, not the material.

relevance.note: Worker:material analogy; MTS

questions.question: Three of the following four numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: 23, 29 and 37 are prime numbers; 51 = 3 × 17 is not.

relevance.note: Composite 51 among primes; MTS odd-number classic trap

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'tom pit sur' means 'good red apple' and 'sur lam pit' means 'red sweet apple'. Which code stands for 'good'?
questions.explanation: 'pit' and 'sur' are common to both and stand for 'red' and 'apple'. So in the first sentence 'tom' means 'good'.

relevance.note: Sentence coding by elimination; MTS

questions.question:
If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' for '×', 'C' for '+' and 'D' for '−', what is the value of the following expression?
36 A 4 B 3 C 8 D 5

relevance.note: Letter-for-sign BODMAS; MTS

questions.question: If 1 January 2026 was a Thursday, what day of the week was 1 March 2026?
questions.explanation: January has 31 days and February 2026 has 28: 59 days = 8 weeks + 3 days. Thursday + 3 = Sunday.

relevance.note: Day of 1 March from 1 Jan 2026 (correct calendar); MTS

questions.question: A clock shows the time 2:15. What time will its image show in a plane mirror placed vertically in front of it?

relevance.note: Mirror time 11:60 rule; MTS

questions.question: The Satpura Range lies between which two rivers?
questions.explanation: The Satpura Range lies between the Narmada (north) and the Tapi (south).

relevance.note: Satpura between Narmada and Tapi; MTS geography

questions.question: In which year was the Planning Commission of India set up?
questions.explanation: The Planning Commission was set up in March 1950; the First Five-Year Plan began in 1951. It was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.

relevance.note: Planning Commission 1950 with 1951 plan trap; MTS economy

questions.question: The construction of the Qutub Minar in Delhi was started by which ruler?
questions.explanation: Qutb-ud-din Aibak began the Qutub Minar; Iltutmish completed the upper storeys.

relevance.note: Qutub Minar started by Aibak with Iltutmish trap; MTS

questions.question: Which Indian chess player became the youngest-ever World Chess Champion by winning the title in December 2024?
questions.explanation: D. Gukesh beat Ding Liren in Singapore in December 2024, becoming world champion at 18.

relevance.note: Gukesh Dec 2024 world title; recent CA asked in MTS 2025

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error, or 'No error'.
We discussed about / the problem / for an hour
questions.explanation: 'Discuss' is a transitive verb and does not take 'about': 'We discussed the problem for an hour.'

relevance.note: 'Discussed about' redundancy; classic SSC error

questions.question: What is the least number which, when divided by 12, 15 and 20, leaves a remainder of 7 in each case?
questions.explanation: LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60. Required number = 60 + 7 = 67.

questions.question: The price of rice rises by 20%. By what percentage must a family reduce its consumption so that its expenditure on rice remains the same?
In an election between two candidates, one candidate got 60% of the votes polled and won by 1,200 votes. How many votes were polled in all? (All votes were valid.)
questions.explanation: Winning margin = 60% − 40% = 20% of total = 1,200 ⇒ total = 6,000.

questions.question: A man buys pens at 12 for ₹100 and sells them at 10 for ₹100. What is his profit percentage?
What is the compound interest on ₹8,000 for 2 years at 5% per annum, compounded annually?
If A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 6 : 7, what is A : B : C?
questions.explanation: Make B common: A : B = 9 : 12 and B : C = 12 : 14. So A : B : C = 9 : 12 : 14.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 10 days and B can do it in 15 days. With the help of C, they finish the work in 5 days. In how many days can C alone do the work?
questions.explanation: C's one-day work = 1/5 − 1/10 − 1/15 = (6 − 3 − 2)/30 = 1/30. So C alone takes 30 days.

questions.question: A train 180 m long crosses a platform 120 m long in 15 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.explanation: Distance = 180 + 120 = 300 m; speed = 300/15 = 20 m/s = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h. Using only the train length gives 43.2 km/h.

questions.question: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is 26 cm and one of the other sides is 10 cm. What is the area of the triangle?
questions.explanation: Third side = √(26² − 10²) = √576 = 24 cm. Area = ½ × 10 × 24 = 120 cm².

questions.question: How many cubes of edge 3 cm can be cut from a cuboid measuring 9 cm × 12 cm × 15 cm?

Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number.
(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits.)
6 : 222 :: 4 : ? :: 5 : 130

Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster.
BDF : CFI :: GIK : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +2, +3: B→C, D→F, F→I. So G→H, I→K, K→N = HKN.

questions.question: Three of the following four words are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: Kathakali, Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi are classical dances; Bhangra is a folk dance of Punjab.

questions.question: Three of the following four letter-pairs are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd letter-pair.
questions.explanation: D–W, F–U and H–S are opposite-letter pairs (positions add up to 27). J's opposite is Q, not R.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'MOTHER' is written as 'NNUGFQ'. How will 'SISTER' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Letters are shifted alternately +1 and −1: M+1=N, O−1=N, T+1=U, H−1=G, E+1=F, R−1=Q. SISTER → T, H, T, S, F, Q.

questions.question: Pointing to a man, Kavita said, "He is the son of my mother's only brother." How is the man related to Kavita?
questions.explanation: Kavita's mother's only brother is her maternal uncle; his son is Kavita's cousin.

questions.question: Ajay is facing North. He turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise and then 45° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: North → (90° clockwise) East → (180° anticlockwise) West → (45° clockwise) North-West.

questions.question:
Which two mathematical signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?
9 + 63 ÷ 7 × 5 − 8 = 78
In a row of 35 students, Ravi is 11th from the left end and Sunil is 15th from the right end. How many students are there between Ravi and Sunil?
questions.explanation: Sunil is 35 − 15 + 1 = 21st from the left. Students between = 21 − 11 − 1 = 9.

questions.question:
Statements:
All doctors are teachers.
No teacher is a singer.
Conclusions:
I. No doctor is a singer.
II. Some singers are teachers.
Which conclusion(s) follow(s)?
questions.explanation: Doctors lie inside teachers, which are wholly separate from singers, so no doctor is a singer (I follows). II contradicts 'No teacher is a singer'.

questions.question: The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was built by which Mughal emperor?
questions.explanation: Akbar built the Buland Darwaza (c. 1575) to commemorate his victory over Gujarat.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Harshacharita', the biography of King Harshavardhana?
questions.explanation: Banabhatta, the court poet of Harsha, wrote Harshacharita and Kadambari. Harisena wrote the Prayag Prashasti.

questions.question: The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn by Mahatma Gandhi in 1922 after which incident?
questions.explanation: After a mob set fire to a police station at Chauri Chaura (February 1922), Gandhi called off the movement.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment?
questions.explanation: Article 16 deals with equality of opportunity in public employment. Article 14 is equality before law; Article 15 prohibits discrimination.

questions.question: The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

questions.question: What is the term of office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
options: 5 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
6 years or up to 62 years of age, whichever is earlier
6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
questions.explanation: The CAG holds office for six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.

questions.question: By what name is the river Brahmaputra known in Tibet?
questions.explanation: It is called Tsangpo in Tibet, Dihang/Siang in Arunachal Pradesh and Jamuna in Bangladesh.

questions.question: In which layer of the atmosphere do almost all weather phenomena such as clouds and rain occur?
questions.explanation: The troposphere, the lowest layer, contains almost all water vapour, so weather occurs there.

questions.question: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the portion of deposits that commercial banks must keep:
options: with the Reserve Bank of India
in gold and approved securities with themselves
with the State Bank of India
questions.explanation: CRR is held as cash balance with the RBI. Keeping liquid assets such as gold and government securities with themselves is SLR.

questions.question: Which Five-Year Plan of India was based on the Mahalanobis model?
questions.explanation: The Second Plan (1956–61) followed the P. C. Mahalanobis model with emphasis on heavy industry. The First Plan used the Harrod–Domar model.

questions.question: Which type of lens is used to correct myopia (short-sightedness)?
questions.explanation: In myopia the image forms in front of the retina; a concave (diverging) lens corrects it. Hypermetropia is corrected with a convex lens.

questions.question: What is the chemical name of bleaching powder?
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is calcium oxychloride (CaOCl₂).

questions.question: Which vitamin is essential for the clotting of blood?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is needed to make clotting factors such as prothrombin.

questions.question: The loss of water in the form of vapour from the aerial parts of a plant is called:
questions.explanation: Transpiration is loss of water vapour, mainly through stomata. Guttation is loss of water as liquid drops.

questions.question: 'Yakshagana' is a traditional dance-drama form of which state?
questions.explanation: Yakshagana is the theatre form of coastal Karnataka.

questions.question: The Charminar in Hyderabad was built by:
questions.explanation: Sultan Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of the Qutb Shahi dynasty built the Charminar in 1591.

questions.question: Which country hosted the 17th BRICS Summit in July 2025?
questions.explanation: The 17th BRICS Summit was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in July 2025. Russia hosted the 16th summit (Kazan, 2024).

questions.question: Which Indian chess player won the FIDE Women's World Cup in July 2025?
questions.explanation: 19-year-old Divya Deshmukh beat Koneru Humpy in the final at Batumi, Georgia, and also became a Grandmaster.

questions.question: The term 'bully' is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: A 'bully' is used to start or restart play in field hockey.

questions.question: Who is the author of the novel 'The Guide'?
questions.explanation: 'The Guide' (1958) by R. K. Narayan won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1960.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.

The postal service is one of the oldest public services in India. For more than a century and a half, the postman has carried letters, money orders and parcels to the remotest villages, often walking long distances in heat and rain. With the arrival of mobile phones and e-mail, many people believed that the post office would soon become useless. Yet India Post has adapted to the new age. Today it runs a bank, the India Post Payments Bank, which helps people in villages receive money and pensions at their doorstep. Post offices also deliver a huge number of parcels for online shopping companies. In this way, an old institution has found new reasons to remain important in people's lives.

What did many people believe after the arrival of mobile phones and e-mail?
options: That the post office would soon become useless
That postmen would walk longer distances
That letters would become more popular
That parcels would no longer be sent
questions.explanation: The passage says many people believed the post office would soon become useless.

options: It gives them free mobile phones
It lets them receive money and pensions at their doorstep

questions.question:
Read the passage and select the most appropriate option for the numbered blank.

Trees are our best friends. They give us fresh air, fruit and shade, and they are home (1) ______ many birds and animals. Their roots hold the soil together and (2) ______ it from being washed away by rain. Sadly, a large number of trees are cut down every year to make room for roads and buildings. We cannot stop development, (3) ______ we can plant more trees to make up for the loss. If every student plants a sapling and (4) ______ after it for just one year, our towns will become (5) ______ and healthier.

Select the most appropriate option for blank (1).
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'home to': the trees are home to many birds.

questions.question:
Read the passage and select the most appropriate option for the numbered blank.

Trees are our best friends. They give us fresh air, fruit and shade, and they are home (1) ______ many birds and animals. Their roots hold the soil together and (2) ______ it from being washed away by rain. Sadly, a large number of trees are cut down every year to make room for roads and buildings. We cannot stop development, (3) ______ we can plant more trees to make up for the loss. If every student plants a sapling and (4) ______ after it for just one year, our towns will become (5) ______ and healthier.

Select the most appropriate option for blank (2).
questions.explanation: 'Prevent something from happening' is the correct pattern; 'avoid', 'refuse' and 'deny' do not take 'it from'.

questions.question:
Read the passage and select the most appropriate option for the numbered blank.

Trees are our best friends. They give us fresh air, fruit and shade, and they are home (1) ______ many birds and animals. Their roots hold the soil together and (2) ______ it from being washed away by rain. Sadly, a large number of trees are cut down every year to make room for roads and buildings. We cannot stop development, (3) ______ we can plant more trees to make up for the loss. If every student plants a sapling and (4) ______ after it for just one year, our towns will become (5) ______ and healthier.

Select the most appropriate option for blank (3).
questions.explanation: The two clauses contrast (cannot stop development / can plant trees), so 'but' is needed.

questions.question:
Read the passage and select the most appropriate option for the numbered blank.

Trees are our best friends. They give us fresh air, fruit and shade, and they are home (1) ______ many birds and animals. Their roots hold the soil together and (2) ______ it from being washed away by rain. Sadly, a large number of trees are cut down every year to make room for roads and buildings. We cannot stop development, (3) ______ we can plant more trees to make up for the loss. If every student plants a sapling and (4) ______ after it for just one year, our towns will become (5) ______ and healthier.

Select the most appropriate option for blank (4).
questions.explanation: 'Look after' means take care of. 'Take after' means resemble, and 'care' takes 'for', not 'after'.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
ABANDON
questions.explanation: Abandon means to leave behind – desert. 'Dessert' is a look-alike; 'adopt' and 'retain' are opposites.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
FRAGILE
questions.explanation: Fragile means easily broken – delicate. 'Sturdy' is the opposite and 'fragrant' a look-alike.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
TEMPORARY
questions.explanation: The opposite of temporary is permanent; the other options are synonyms of temporary.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
GENUINE
questions.explanation: Genuine means real; its opposite is fake. Authentic and real are synonyms.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To bite off more than one can chew
options: To take on a task that is too big for one
questions.explanation: The idiom means to attempt more than one can manage; 'to eat too quickly' is the literal reading.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To hit the nail on the head
options: To finish work in a hurry
questions.explanation: 'Hit the nail on the head' means to say or do exactly the right thing.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A person who loves and collects books
questions.explanation: A bibliophile loves books. A bibliographer compiles lists of books; a philanthropist helps others.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
questions.explanation: The agenda lists items to be discussed; the minutes record what was discussed after the meeting.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'tomorrow' – one 'm' and double 'r'.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error, or 'No error'.
The furniture in these rooms / are very old / and needs repair.
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb: 'is very old'.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error, or 'No error'.
If I will get leave / I will visit / my grandparents.
questions.explanation: In a first conditional the if-clause takes the simple present: 'If I get leave, I will visit…'.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Neither the teacher nor the students ______ present in the class yesterday.
questions.explanation: With 'neither…nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('students', plural) and the time is past: 'were'.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The police ______ a case against the shopkeeper for selling fake medicines.
questions.explanation: Police 'register' a case (FIR). The other words do not collocate with 'case' in this sense.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bracketed part of the sentence.
I prefer tea [than] coffee.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' is followed by 'to': I prefer tea to coffee.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bracketed part of the sentence.
The bus [has left] before we reached the stop.
questions.explanation: Of two past actions, the earlier one takes the past perfect: 'The bus had left before we reached'.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The teacher will check the answer sheets.
options: The answer sheets would be checked by the teacher.
The answer sheets will be checked by the teacher.
The answer sheets will have been checked by the teacher.
The answer sheets are checked by the teacher.
questions.explanation: Simple future active 'will check' becomes 'will be checked' in the passive.
